rows.source: OPSS button and coin battery safety
rows.verified: Button and coin batteries can cause life-threatening injury when swallowed, particularly in young children and vulnerable adults.

rows.source: OPSS button and coin battery safety
rows.verified: Coin batteries are generally larger and lithium-powered and can present a greater ingestion hazard than smaller button batteries.

rows.source: OPSS button and coin battery safety
rows.verified: Tissue damage may begin within about two hours after a button battery is swallowed.

rows.source: OPSS button and coin battery safety
rows.verified: Symptoms of button-battery ingestion may be non-specific, making rapid recognition difficult.

rows.source: OPSS button and coin battery safety
rows.verified: OPSS sponsored PAS 7055:2021, a standard addressing battery design, product casing, packaging and safe retailing.

rows.source: OPSS button and coin battery safety
rows.verified: Consumers should check toys, lights, remote controls and other products for accessible or loose button batteries.

rows.source: OPSS button and coin battery safety
rows.verified: Products with loose backs or batteries that can fall out should be secured or removed from children's reach.

rows.source: OPSS button and coin battery safety
rows.verified: OPSS research has examined prevention, detection and reactive technologies intended to reduce ingestion harm.

rows.source: OPSS button and coin battery safety
rows.verified: Button-battery risk depends on battery chemistry and size, product enclosure, accessibility, user age, ingestion timing and clinical response.

rows.source: OPSS button and coin battery safety
rows.verified: OPSS button-battery evidence is battery-, product-, user-, exposure-, clinical- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury probability.

rows.source: OPSS e-bike and e-scooter lithium-battery safety
rows.verified: Lithium-ion batteries used in e-bikes and e-scooters can cause serious fire or explosion when unsafe, damaged, modified or improperly charged.

rows.source: OPSS e-bike and e-scooter lithium-battery safety
rows.verified: Consumers should buy e-bikes, batteries and chargers from known sellers and check product information before purchase.

rows.source: OPSS e-bike and e-scooter lithium-battery safety
rows.verified: Only manufacturer-recommended batteries, chargers and replacement parts should be used.

rows.source: OPSS e-bike and e-scooter lithium-battery safety
rows.verified: Charging should take place in a safe location that does not block escape routes.

rows.source: OPSS e-bike and e-scooter lithium-battery safety
rows.verified: Chargers should be unplugged when charging is complete and devices should not be left charging unattended or while occupants are asleep.

rows.source: OPSS e-bike and e-scooter lithium-battery safety
rows.verified: A battery or charger should be taken out of use if it overheats, deforms, hisses, cracks, smells, smokes or performs abnormally.

rows.source: OPSS e-bike and e-scooter lithium-battery safety
rows.verified: Battery modification or tampering should not be attempted, and conversion or repair work should be performed by a competent professional.

rows.source: OPSS e-bike and e-scooter lithium-battery safety
rows.verified: OPSS statutory guidelines require producers and distributors to consider safety mechanisms addressing thermal runaway in e-bike batteries.

rows.source: OPSS e-bike and e-scooter lithium-battery safety
rows.verified: E-bike battery risk depends on cell quality, battery-management design, charger compatibility, damage, modification, storage, charging behaviour and escape conditions.

rows.source: OPSS e-bike and e-scooter lithium-battery safety
rows.verified: OPSS e-bike evidence is product-, battery-, charger-, user-, premises- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level fire probability.
